messages:
ryan: Heads-up — I just saw an unexpected RBAC change on prod-cluster-3. cluster-admin binding created on svcacct-dataflow @svc-dataflow-prod at 14:02 UTC. No change request in changelog.

opsbot: Incident created INC-2026-042 by ryan at 14:03 UTC. Channel #inc-2003007777 opened.

dawn: ack. can you paste the audit event id and any kube-apiserver logs you have? I want to know whether it was via kubectl or via API.

ryan: logs snip:
```
I0414 14:02:11.123456 1 admission.go:123] user="system:serviceaccount:infra:deploy-bot" verb="create" resource="clusterrolebinding" name="svcacct-dataflow-cluster-admin" subresource="" requestURI="/apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1/clusterrolebindings"
```
Audit ID: 9b7f6c2e-....
No matching entry in our change control system.

miguel: odd — that user is ephemeral and usually limited. checking vault/OIDC logs for that SA token issuance.

jess: looking at KMS logs, we have a small decrypt spike around 14:01 UTC from the same IP range as build runners. KMS key alias: alias/redwood-prod-secrets. I can pull CloudTrail entries.

secops-oncall: +1. If KMS decrypts happened and then a cluster-admin binding was created, we need to assume potential credential compromise. Contain first: revoke that service account tokens and any recently minted K8s tokens, rotate the SA keys, and block the runner IP ranges.

ryan: I removed the binding and created a deny-all temporary policy on the node pool (taints + network ACL) at 14:07 UTC so no new agent can act as that SA. I also created a pod disruption to prevent rollout. Commands run:
```
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding svcacct-dataflow-cluster-admin
kubectl annotate namespace dataflow security-temporary-block=true
```

dawn: good. miguel, can you confirm whether the SA private key was exported or if an external token exchange happened? Check KMS Decrypt events for GenerateDataKey/Decrypt with keyId matching alias. Also check STS AssumeRole or OIDC token endpoint logs.

miguel: quick triage: found 3 Decrypt calls between 14:00-14:02 from IP 34.217.55.12. The caller identity is compute-engine@redwood-ci. The runner job id matches a merge from repo infra/automation that had a workflow change two hours ago. I'm pulling the job payload to see if it had a leaked secret.

jess: CloudTrail shows a ConsoleLogin and then two GenerateDataKey calls from the same account within 2m. No explicit KMS Grant created. KMS Key policy hasn't changed. I'm exporting the raw events to /tmp/inc-2003007777-kms.json

secops-oncall: Action list so far: 1) revoke SA tokens, 2) delete clusterrolebinding (done), 3) block runner IP, 4) rotate KMS data key for alias/redwood-prod-secrets (planned), 5) snapshot etcd and kube-apiserver audit logs, 6) preserve CI runner VM, 7) notify legal if exfil suspected. Who owns KMS rotation? jess/miguel?

jess: I can start a staged key rotation but prefer to snapshot current decrypt logs first. Miguel — hold the VM; I'll trigger rotation after we get a snapshot and a signed handoff.

miguel: holding VM, extracting job artifacts now. Found a base64 blob in artifacts that decodes to a KMS-encrypted payload; looks like it contains a service principal token. Uploading evidence to /vault/incidents/INC-2026-042/artifacts.

ryan: I'm creating a short timeline in the war-room doc: root cause unclear, likely CI runner leaked artifact -> used to call KMS decrypt -> used to create RBAC binding. Root/next steps: forensics, rotate keys, patch workflow to remove secrets, audit all service accounts in last 24h.

dawn: I'm drafting a pagerduty escalation to SRE infra lead and Legal (per policy for potential creds exfil). Also adding the exec summary for product security.

secops-oncall: We're going to treat as confirmed compromise until proven otherwise. Keep all evidence preserved and avoid rotating keys prematurely until we snapshot. Postmortem owner? ryan volunteer?

ryan: i'll own the postmortem. For handoff to next oncall (starting 20:00 UTC) — Summary: cluster-admin binding created and removed, KMS decrypt spike correlated with CI runner. Evidence path: /vault/incidents/INC-2026-042. Actions pending: full KMS rotation (jess), CI credentials rotation and workflow rollback (miguel), legal notif (dawn), forensics snapshots (secops-oncall). No external communication yet.

dawn: handoff checklist added to the doc. Next oncall please confirm: 1) no other RBAC changes after 14:07, 2) VM preserved, 3) KMS snapshot uploaded, 4) rotation timeline agreed. Tagging @secops-oncall for followup.

opsbot: Handoff: incident INC-2026-042 transferred from ryan to secops-oncall at 14:40 UTC. Next oncall shift assigned secops-oncall.

secops-oncall: ack takeover. I'll run a quick verification sweep and ping if anything escalates. Leaving the channel open for the investigation. :lock:

jess: uploaded KMS event dump and started staged rotation plan in the doc. ETA for rotation proposal: 2 hours.

miguel: CI workflow reverted and token issuance disabled for merge jobs as temporary mitigation.

ryan: thanks team. logging out — please update the doc with any new findings. I'll post the postmortem draft tomorrow.
